text.p: Spanish government bonds sank at the close in a market unwilling to carry heavy positions which might be vulnerable to negative data during Friday's holiday.
"Non-farm jobs data in the U.S. is published tomorrow and people are fearful of what could happen with this indicator with the Spanish market closed," one dealer said.
Dollar weakness added to the selling urge, which was compounded by recent auctions that left traders with a lot of paper on their hands ahead of a holiday.
Apart from holiday-driven trade, dealers said the market was fundamentally sound.
The spread over Germany's benchmark was 131, unchanged from yesterday, as expectations of a rate cut in December underpinned the Spanish market despite holiday jitters.
"That the market took advantage of the festival to correct itself after such climbs isn't unwelcome," one dealer said.
